metadata.title: Supernova Shocks Cannot Explain the Inflated State of Hypervelocity Runaways from White Dwarf Binaries

the fastest ones being ≈ 2500 km s<sup>−1</sup>. As they are unbound
to the Galaxy and still observable

evidence.quote: All the observed D<sup>6</sup> runaway candidates are peculiar. They have galactocentric velocities greater than 1000 km s<sup>−1</sup>

notes:
General roster note: these are observed D6 candidate runaways adopted from prior literature, not candidates newly discovered by this paper; the 0.50–1.10 M⊙ donor models are not additional stars. The group unbound statement is at T:p1-b18, the model comparison at T:p8-b7, and the member list plus prior-data attribution at T:p9-b10.
D6-1: one of the cooler D6-1,2,3 candidates attributed to Chandra et al. (2022) and Shen et al. (2018a) (T:p8-b3, T:p8-b9); no full catalog identifier is supplied.
D6-2: the slowest Table 3 entry but still explicitly a listed D6 candidate runaway (T:p9-b10); no full catalog identifier is supplied.
D6-3: one of the cooler D6-1,2,3 candidates (T:p8-b9) and a Table 3 entry (T:p9-b10); no full catalog identifier is supplied.
J1235: parameters are cited from El-Badry et al. (2023), and it is listed as a D6 candidate runaway (T:p8-b9, T:p9-b10); no full catalog identifier is supplied.
J0927: listed as a D6 candidate runaway (T:p9-b10); no full catalog identifier is supplied.
J0546: listed as a D6 candidate runaway (T:p9-b10); the “J3546” in the Fig. B.1 caption (T:p14-b1) is an apparent typo for J0546 because that figure labels J0546 (I:p14-b0), so no separate J3546 is listed.
J1332: listed as a D6 candidate runaway and discussed as the only object consistent with the cooling track (T:p8-b11, T:p9-b10); its consistency with the cooling track does not remove its status as a previously identified follow-up candidate. The “J332” in T:p8-b3 is an apparent typo for J1332, so no separate J332 is listed.

D6-1: The only individual value reported for D6-1 is its ejection velocity in Table 3. The paper does not explicitly label it as a Galactic-rest-frame speed, but it treats these unbound runaways as having galactocentric/ejection velocities; no separate radial velocity or other velocity components are given for D6-1. No coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability are reported for D6-1.

D6-2: D6-2 is discussed in the paper, but no eligible quantity from the required list is reported for it. Table 3 (T:p9-b10; also I:p9-b10) gives an ejection velocity of 1051^{+62}_{-54} km/s and donor masses of 0.1 M_sun, but ejection velocity is not a line-of-sight heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, and mass is not a requested quantity. The age discussion at T:p7-b12 and the figure/table discussions at T:p9-b2, T:p9-b8, and T:p8-b9 do not report right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for D6-2.

D6-3: D6-3 appears in Table 3 (T:p9-b10) with an ejection velocity of 2393^{+377}_{-391} km/s and donor-mass estimates, but ejection velocity is not one of the eligible quantities and is not explicitly identified as the present-day total Galactic rest-frame speed. No right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported specifically for D6-3.

J1235: J1235 is discussed as an observed D6 hypervelocity runaway. The paper does not report its individual right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, line-of-sight radial velocity, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability. Table 3 gives its ejection velocity as 2471 +351/-345 km/s (adopted from El-Badry et al. 2023); this is the only star-specific speed reported for J1235 and is recorded here as the total Galactic rest-frame speed. Its donor-mass estimates in that table (0.8 and 1.1 solar masses) are not among the requested quantities.

J0927: J0927 is only reported with an ejection velocity (2519 +271/-147 km/s) and donor-mass estimates in Table 3 (T:p9-b10), plus a qualitative statement that it is "coming towards us" (T:p7-b12). No equatorial coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, line-of-sight radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star. The ejection velocity is a total velocity relative to the pre-supernova binary, not a heliocentric/barycentric line-of-sight radial velocity, so it is not recorded under the listed quantity definitions.

J0546: Table 3 (T:p9-b10, I:p9-b10) also reports J0546 minimum and estimated donor masses of 0.2 and 0.7 M⊙, but mass is not one of the requested quantity identifiers. The paper does not report individual RA, Dec, distance, parallax, proper motions, line-of-sight radial velocity, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probabilities for J0546.

J1332: Table 3 labels the J1332 velocity as V_ejection rather than explicitly as a Galactic-rest-frame speed, so this mapping is the closest eligible quantity. The paper also reports for J1332 donor-mass estimates (M_min=0.2 Msun, M_est=0.4 Msun), a mid-plane age of about 0.6 Myr, and that it is the only observed D6 star consistent with the model tracks; these are not among the allowed quantity identifiers. No equatorial coordinates, distance/parallax, proper motion, line-of-sight radial velocity, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability for J1332 is reported in the supplied material.
